args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api started failing health checks after the latest production deploy, v2.3.1. Before the rollback it was marked unhealthy with an error rate of 18% in all regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). v2.3.1-rc had also been marked unhealthy in staging. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Checked after the rollback: all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy, and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying it, and look at why it was promoted when the rc was unhealthy in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened the SEV2 incident.

- **Version picked:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1, the latest deploy, is the one failing. Its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) only ever ran in staging, so it didn't count.
- **Rollback:** us-east, us-west and eu-west all moved from v2.3.1 to v2.3.0.
- **Check afterwards:** the service reports healthy, and the error rate dropped from 18% to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and the on-call engineer has been paged. It says what failed, what I did, the numbers before and after, and next steps. Those are: find the root cause in v2.3.1 before redeploying it, and look into why it went to production when its release candidate had already failed in staging.

The first attempt to create the incident timed out. The incident list showed nothing had been created, so I tried again using the same request ID, which stops a duplicate from being made. Only one incident exists.
